title: OOFEM simulation eval
summary: Can a model write a Python script against the OOFEM bindings that reproduces a paper's curves? There is no spec to compare: the script runs, and the curves it writes are scored against the paper's digitized data. The default one-shot arm gets one call with no repair loop. The agent arm (--agent) can read the OOFEM source, try things in a sandbox and validate its script before submitting.

groups.label: one-shot arm (default)
groups.detail: Used when --agent is not given. One call, no feedback of any kind: the script runs once as written.

groups.label: agent arm
groups.detail: A tool loop that runs until the model submits a validated script or a budget runs out. The full transcript is kept, so every step can be audited.

groups.label: agent tools
groups.detail: Reads are confined to the OOFEM tree and the workdir; writes to the workdir.

nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.detail: Paper text, paper PDF and scope.md per case. Built automatically if missing.

nodes.label: Reference curves
nodes.detail: The (file, column) curves a case must reproduce. The prompt and the scorer use the same list, so they cannot drift apart. Cases without reference curves are skipped before any call.

nodes.label: OOFEM source + API
nodes.detail: The bindings' API list and example scripts. The agent arm can also read the C++ source, where the input keywords are defined.

nodes.label: Model roster
nodes.detail: Model ids, token limits, timeouts, prices, and whether a model accepts images.

nodes.label: oofempy importable
nodes.detail: OOFEM_PY can import the compiled bindings. Checked before any call; skipped by --dry-run.

nodes.label: Build prompt
nodes.detail: Scope, paper text (cut at --max-paper-chars), the curve contract (ids, x ranges, units), the API list and examples, and the time limit the script must fit.

nodes.label: Write script
nodes.detail: One chat completion. The reply must contain the whole script.

nodes.label: Extract Python
nodes.detail: The first fenced block that parses as Python becomes candidate.py. Otherwise the outcome is unparseable and nothing runs.

nodes.label: Static gate
nodes.detail: Refuses scripts that import subprocess, socket, urllib and similar, or that never import oofempy. Outcome rejected.

nodes.label: Run script
nodes.detail: Runs candidate.py with OOFEM_PY in a fresh work/ directory that holds the reference CSVs. Outcomes: crashed (with the signal, e.g. SIGSEGV inside oofem), timeout, or no results.csv.

nodes.label: System prompt + workdir
nodes.detail: A small fixed system prompt: scope, curve contract, API list, turn budget. The paper goes into work/ as paper.txt and paper.pdf, not into the prompt, so forty turns don't repeat 400k characters.

nodes.label: Agent turn
nodes.detail: One completion per turn with tool calls. Token use is added up across turns and reported next to the score, along with the cost when models.yaml has a price.

nodes.label: Turn budget + nudges
nodes.detail: A first candidate.py is due after a third of --max-turns, insisted on at half. After --max-turns, --finalization-turns remain for repair, validation and submit only. The loop stops on submit, when the budget runs out, after more than 3 turns in a row without a tool call, on degenerate repeated output, or on an API error that persists through --api-retries.

nodes.label: Read OOFEM source
nodes.detail: list_dir, read_file, grep, inspect_oofem.

nodes.label: Read paper
nodes.detail: read_paper_page for text. view_paper_page renders the page as an image, only for models marked vision.

nodes.label: run_python
nodes.detail: Short experiments against the bindings, each capped by --spike-timeout.

nodes.label: write_file
nodes.detail: Writes candidate.py (or scratch files). Writing candidate.py marks it as not validated.

nodes.label: run_candidate
nodes.detail: Runs candidate.py from a clean staging directory, so leftovers from a spike can't help it pass, and checks that results.csv holds the contract's curve ids. Capped by --run-timeout.

nodes.label: submit
nodes.detail: Accepted only if this exact candidate.py passed run_candidate. An edit after that makes the submission invalid again.

nodes.label: results.csv + plot
nodes.detail: Long format, curve,x,y, because the curves of one case can have different x axes. The script must also plot its result over the reference.

nodes.label: Score curves
nodes.detail: The simulation is interpolated onto the reference x samples. score = coverage × max(0, 1 − nrmse). A missing curve scores 0; extra curves don't count.

nodes.label: run.json
nodes.detail: Per call: mode, outcome, curve scores, turns, tokens, cost, and whether the final script really used oofempy (solver_evidence).

edges.carries: reference/ copied into work/ for the overlay plot

edges.label: nudges + stop
edges.carries: 'candidate.py is due now', 'finalization only: N turns remain', and the stop decision
exit status, run time, missing curve ids, the tail of the output
only the contract outputs, copied back

params.help: Which models to call. Default: the entries marked default in models.yaml.
Which cases to run. Default: every case with a paper and reference curves.
Stop after the first N selected cases.
The OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Default: endpoint in models.yaml.
Cut the paper text in the one-shot prompt. The agent arm always gets the full paper as a file.
Seconds per API call, overriding models.yaml. Matters most for the agent, which makes one call per turn.
Use the agent arm instead of the one-shot arm.
Normal turns for exploring, writing and repairing.
Extra turns after --max-turns that may only repair, validate and submit an existing candidate.
Retries of one turn after a transient API failure.
Seconds allowed for one run_python experiment.
Seconds allowed for one full simulation run.
Build the prompt (or the agent's system prompt) and write it to prompt.md. Calls nothing; needs no oofempy.
Re-score an existing run's outputs. No calls, no solving.
Print the curves each case must produce, then exit.
One-line description, used by worker.sh to list the jobs.
